Background (from the session that started this one):
This continues a long research session on "imbrication", reading binary sequences through sliding windows. It ended up studying lossless storage of a model version against a related one.

Established and committed:
- The saving depends on drift between versions (one law across 11 pairs). Checkpoints and fine-tunes save 20–30%; independent seeds save nothing, even after permutation or rotation alignment.
- The ordered-integer difference beats XOR.
- Low-order bits are noise.
- In simulation, low-precision formats save fewer bits but a larger share: NVFP4 ~0.25× coding alone.

An outside counsel and a full reading of ULPack (2026) showed that everything except the format question is already published (FM-Delta 2024, ULPack 2026). A bug was also fixed: FP16 values occupy 19 bits of F32, not 16.

The user wants real quantized pairs measured before proposing anything to their Rust org mi-for-the-rust-of-us; anamnesis is the natural home for the feature.

House rules:
- Reports must state the motivating question and hypotheses with verdicts.
- Follow weak signals rather than taking requests as literal orders.
- Use the waiting-on-processes skill for long jobs.
- Never pkill by name.
- Downloaded weights go in data/raw/ (gitignored; 2.2 GB of Pythia and MultiBERTs files are already there).

Task:
In /Users/hacker/Documents/explore/combinatorics_on_binary, decide whether lossless reference coding of model weights has a future beyond the published work, by measuring it on REAL quantized model pairs rather than simulations.

Read first: __reports__/reference_coding/README.md, then 08-paper_analysis_ulpack_v0.md, 07-counsel_v0.md, 06-findings_v6.md (the format simulation) and 02-findings_v2.md (the MLX 8-bit pairs). Code is in code/delta/: mlx_pair.py, formats.py, f32_delta.py, topk_shotgun.py and st.py.

Probes to run:
1. Real MLX 8-bit sibling pairs already on disk in ~/.lmstudio/models (Ministral-3 3B/8B/14B Instruct vs Reasoning, LFM2.5 Instruct vs Thinking). Re-measure the code and scale streams with a ULPack-style coder: ordered-integer residuals, conditioned on the reference's own value or exponent, entropy-coded. Compare against what was measured in v2 (zstd on byte planes).
2. Real GGUF and/or NVFP4 pairs of one model family, at the same quantization, from two related checkpoints (base vs instruct, or two checkpoints). Find candidates with hf-fetch-model (hf-fm search / inspect / quants) or ~/.lmstudio/models, before downloading anything. Ask the user before any download, stating file names and sizes. Parse and dequantize with the Rust crate anamnesis (github.com/mi-for-the-rust-of-us/anamnesis, CLI `amn`) or your own reader.
3. Test the one claim still open in the literature (ULPack, arXiv 2610.14184, lists float8 as untested): low-precision formats gain more from a reference, in relative terms. Use real pairs, with scales counted, real compressed byte counts, and a decode round trip verified.

Done means: a findings report __reports__/reference_coding/09-findings_v7.md that opens with why it was measured, then hypotheses with verdicts, then an interpretation, then the tables. It must end with a clear go / no-go on proposing a "lossless reference storage across formats" feature to the anamnesis repository. Do not post any issue or PR; draft text only if the verdict is go. Commit following CONTRIBUTING.md.
